articles.title: China October 2026 CPI +0.7% y/y (expected +0.8%, prior +0.9%)
articles.desc: A hot PPI and a soft CPI is a poor mix for China’s growth outlook. It points to margin compression for manufacturers and weak domestic demand, which weighs on sentiment toward Chinese equities and keeps expectations of policy support alive. For the yuan, softer underlying inflation argues for easier
articles.content: A hot PPI and a soft CPI is a poor mix for China’s growth outlook. It points to margin compression for manufacturers and weak domestic demand, which weighs on sentiment toward Chinese equities and keeps expectations of policy support alive. For the yuan, softer underlying inflation argues for easier policy at the margin, a mild negative. For the Australian dollar and commodity currencies, the read is mixed: firm producer prices reflect cost pressure rather than a demand-led recovery in China’s appetite for raw materials. For oil, the PPI surge mainly shows the energy shock feeding through, not new demand strength. --- Earlier: China steps up market stabilisation push: three short-term priorities for equities --- China’s factories are facing their fastest price rises in years while consumer inflation slips further below 1%, a split that points to squeezed margins and fragile domestic demand rather than any healthy reflation. Summary: China’s October PPI rose 5.7% y/y, beating the 5.3% forecast and up from 5% in September. CPI rose 0.7% y/y, below the 0.8% expected and down from 0.9%. CPI was flat month-on-month, in line with forecasts, after a 0.2% rise in September. Core CPI eased to 0.8% from 1%, below the 0.9% forecast. The gap between producer and consumer inflation has widened to around five percentage points. Trade data is due Tuesday, with credit and money supply figures later in the week. China’s factory-gate inflation accelerated more sharply than expected in October, while consumer price growth slowed below forecasts. The result widens the gap between surging producer costs and weak household demand. The producer price index rose 5.7% from a year earlier, well above expectations of around 5.3% and up from 5% in September, when it had already reached a four-year high. Consumer prices increased 0.7% year-on-year, slightly below the 0.8% forecast and down from 0.9% in September. They were flat on the month, in line with expectations, after a 0.2% gain in September. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, eased to 0.8% from 1%, also undershooting forecasts of 0.9%. The divergence between the two measures has now widened to around five percentage points. Producer prices are being driven higher by energy and other input costs, while consumer prices show little sign of following. That suggests manufacturers and retailers are absorbing much of the cost increase rather than passing it on, a reflection of soft domestic demand and limited pricing power. The core reading is the more telling figure for the health of the domestic economy. A slowdown in underlying inflation to below 1% points to subdued demand for services and non-essential goods, despite some support from spending around the National Day Golden Week holiday at the start of October. For policymakers, the mix is awkward. Weak consumer and core inflation strengthens the case for further support for domestic demand. The jump in producer prices, though, limits room for aggressive easing and squeezes industrial profit margins at a time when firms are already facing higher energy costs linked to the war with Iran. The data come as Beijing is also moving to shore up confidence in its stock market, with a recent State Council meeting calling for stronger capital market stabilisation mechanisms. Attention now turns to October trade data due on Tuesday, which will show whether export strength can continue to offset sluggish domestic demand. Credit and money supply figures follow later in the week. --- This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: ‘PH to continue trade with China’
articles.desc: SHANGHAI — The Philippines will continue to engage with China in trade, tourism and people to people exchanges despite their maritime disputes, Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz said Sunday, noting that the two countries’ maritime issues are not the “sum total” of their relations. Speaking to The Manila Tim
articles.content: SHANGHAI — The Philippines will continue to engage with China in trade, tourism and people to people exchanges despite their maritime disputes, Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz said Sunday, noting that the two countries’ maritime issues are not the “sum total” of their relations. Speaking to The Manila Times at the sidelines of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) held at the National Convention and Exhibition Center, FlorCruz said that Manila will continue to engage with Beijing amid their differences. “We differ when we have to, but we engage, we cooperate while we can, and trade and investment, commercial relations are exactly the kind of relations that we need to keep pushing,” he said. “Our maritime issues are not the sum total of our relations, so that means we have to keep on pushing on other fields of our relations,” he added. The Philippines launched on Friday its largest pavilion in the CIIE, comprising over 30 export companies showcasing the country’s food exports, such as coconut products, bananas, durian, and other products. FlorCruz said that trade and investment, alongside tourism and people to people exchanges, are an “important component” of its relations to China. “What we want [is that] the Chinese to succeed in the Philippines in breaking into our market and bringing the best of their products and services. We want them to show that good Philippine-China relations is beneficial to our people, to our markets,” FlorCruz said. Meanwhile, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) welcomed the joint statement of 20 business, labor, industry and civil society organizations supporting diplomacy and dialogue between the Philippines and China. In a statement Saturday evening, the DFA said it “is grateful for the appreciation of these sectors regarding the challenges of diplomatic work.” The DFA said “candor, composure, principled conduct, sound judgment, and measured engagement are vital in the conduct of foreign relations, even as we firmly assert and uphold the Philippines’ rights and entitlements.” The groups earlier commended DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro for her recent “constructive engagement” with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and her call for sustained dialogue and cooperation between the Philippines and China. Lazaro on Tuesday received a telephone call from Wang during which they discussed the state of bilateral ties between Manila and Beijing. “We recognize the DFA’s pragmatic and statesmanlike approach in protecting the country’s national interests, particularly its economic development, trade and exports, tourism, overseas Filipino workers, and other vital bilateral agreements with China, the Philippines’ largest trading partner,” the groups said. “Amid global uncertainty and intensifying economic competition, our Asean (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) neighbors are deepening their trade, investment, technology, infrastructure, and tourism partnerships with China,” they said. The groups said the Philippines “must likewise pursue mutually beneficial economic opportunities through constructive engagement, while firmly upholding its sovereignty and national interests.” In a separate interview with The Manila Times, China Global Television Network digital anchor Shen Shiwei stressed the importance of CIIE for markets such as the Philippines. He said that Philippine companies must remain competitive amid tight competition from Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. Shen said that maritime dispute between Manila and Beijing should not affect negatively on trade relations.

articles.title: Pirates Must Address This Problem This Offseason
articles.desc: The Pittsburgh Pirates spent last offseason doing something they rarely do: investing real money in the lineup. They acquired Brandon Lowe and signed Ryan O'Hea
articles.content: Pirates Must Address This Problem This Offseason | United States Pirates Must Address This Problem This Offseason The Pittsburgh Pirates spent last offseason doing something they rarely do: investing real money in the lineup. They acquired Brandon Lowe and signed Ryan O'Hea Jul 26, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Pirates first baseman Ryan O'Hearn hits a grand slam home run against the Chicago Cubs during the third inning at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Pirates spent last offseason doing something they rarely do: investing real money in the lineup. They acquired Brandon Lowe and signed Ryan O'Hearn, and the result was a franchise-record 182 home runs and a top-five finish in runs scored. For the first time in years, Pittsburgh had an offense that could legitimately compete. The numbers are not subtle. Why Pirates' Brandon Lowe Should Win Silver Slugger Award Pittsburgh went 18-33 when opposing a left-handed starter in 2026, batting .229 with a .300 on-base percentage and a .359 slugging percentage in those games—all dead last in MLB. The club's strikeout rate against southpaws was second-worst in the sport at 25.6%. This wasn't a minor flaw. It was a structural failure that undermined an otherwise encouraging season, and possibly prevented a playoff appearance. The causes are not mysterious. The Pirates built a lineup that leaned heavily left-handed, and the players they acquired to anchor it were precisely the ones who cratered against same-side pitching. Lowe, an All-Star-caliber performer overall, hit .220 with a .632 OPS against lefties compared to a .279 average and .908 OPS against righties. O'Hearn was similarly exposed, and the midseason experiment with Marcell Ozuna—a right-handed bat brought in to help—produced a .207 average against lefties before fizzling entirely. Manager Don Kelly did not pretend otherwise. "It has been an Achilles' heel against lefties," he said in September. He tried the obvious countermeasure in June, rolling out an all-right-handed lineup against Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez. The Pirates managed three hits in seven innings. The problem wasn't just who was in the lineup. It was that too many of the right-handed options weren't good enough to punish lefties either. Nick Gonzales, Jared Triolo, and Henry Davis all posted OPS figures below .700 against southpaws. Sep 29, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Astros third baseman Isaac Paredes hits a single against the Chicago White Sox during game one of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Daikin Park. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This is where the offseason calculus gets uncomfortable. The Pirates have real momentum for the first time since 2018. They have a strong starting rotation, an emerging young core, and a fanbase that has been asked for patience for a very long time. But the free-agent market for right-handed impact bats is thin, and the trade market will likely require parting with the one thing Pittsburgh has in surplus: young pitching. The Pirates do not need another left-handed slugger. They do not need a platoon bat who can only help in ideal matchups. They need awho can start against lefties, stay in the lineup against righties, and prevent opposing managers from lining up a southpaw in a must-win series and knowing, with near certainty, that Pittsburgh's offense will shrink. So who fits that description, and who is actually attainable? The free-agent class offers few clean answers. Eugenio Suárez remains a productive right-handed power bat and would represent the kind of proven middle-of-the-order upgrade the Pirates have avoided pursuing, though his age and strikeout profile make a multi-year commitment risky. articles.title: Thousands remain without power Sunday morning, as Cowichan one of hardest hit regions
articles.content: Thousands remain without power Sunday morning, as Cowichan one of hardest hit regions | Port Alberni Valley News Thousands remain without power Sunday morning, as Cowichan one of hardest hit regions Published 9:09 am Sunday, November 8, 2026 By Andrea Rondeau/Cowichan Valley Citizen Power was out to thousands in the Cowichan Valley on Nov. 7, 2026 due to a windstorm sweeping the area. (screen shot) As of Sunday morning thousands of people remained without power in the Cowichan Valley. New outages overnight included major blackouts in the Cobble Hill (2,080 customers), Shawnigan Lake (2,359), Malahat (2,304) and Saltair (2,244 customers) areas, as well as more of the Cowichan Lake area (more than 2,000 customers). BC Hydro crews said they are working to repair the damage, but more outages could add to the burden before the storm passes completely. “We prepared for this storm and had crews and resources ready to respond immediately,” said Whitney Deane, BC Hydro spokesperson. “Our crews are making good progress, but with strong winds continuing this morning, we expect to see additional damage and outages before conditions improve. We appreciate our customers’ patience as our crews work as quickly and safely as possible to restore power.” At the height of the storm at 1 a.m. Sunday, approximately 135,000 customers were without power, Hydro said. As of 7 a.m. on Sunday, that number has dropped to approximately 63,000 as crews continue restoration efforts. “The hardest-hit areas at this time include Surrey, Duncan, Port Hardy and Prince George, where strong winds have brought down trees and branches, damaging power lines, poles and other electrical equipment,” Hydro said. BC Hydro also had some safety tips for people as B.C. enters the winter season. Customers should stay at least 10 metres away from downed, damaged or low-hanging power lines and call 911 to report them, they said. Customers can get the latest information about outages and estimated restoration times through the new BC Hydro mobile app or at bchydro.com/outages. With additional storms expected, customers are also encouraged to be prepared for potential outages by keeping their 72-hour emergency kits stocked and their mobile devices charged. More information about storm and outage preparedness is available at bchydro.com/safety. A wind and rainstorm has left more than 10,000 Cowichan Valley residents in the dark Saturday night, Nov. 7. As of 9 p.m., outages stretched from Maple Bay to Westholme, Duncan, Ladysmith, Mill Bay and Youbou. Large outages include one described on the BC Hydro website as north of Mays Road affecting 2,131 customers, one stretching from Maple Bay through Genoa Bay, Somenos Road and Quamichan area affecting 2,205 customers, one in the Sahtlam, Hillcrest Road and Paldi areas affecting 1,902 customers, one in the Deerholme area affecting 342 customers, one in south Duncan affecting 1,156 customers, one in the Sherman and Somenos roads area affecting 3,187 customers, one in the Bonsall Road area affection 171 customers, on in Mill Bay affecting 1,777 customers, and several outages in the Youbou, Lake Cowichan and Mesachie Lake areas affecting more than 1,400 customers. A large outage in the Ladysmith area is affecting 1,145 customers. There are also numerous smaller localized outages listed. Numerous outages were also listed up the east coast of Vancouver Island and on the Mainland Saturday night, though Cowichan appears to be the hardest hit area on the Island. The area was under a yellow wind warning, which was expected to last through the night into Sunday morning. Strong southerly winds gusting up to 90km/h were expected. People were advised to secure any loose objects. This is the second big wind and rainstorm to hit the area in the last several days. Cowichan largely escaped power outages during the previous storm. articles.title: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 4 and injures 88
articles.desc: Egyptian authorities say at least four people were killed and 88 others were injured when a train traveling between Giza and Fayoum collided with another train traveling from Cairo to Aswan
articles.content: Train collision in Egypt's Giza province leaves 7 dead and 125 injured, officials say - WSB-TV Channel 2 - Atlanta Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125 AL-AYYAT, Egypt — Two trains collided Sunday south of the capital of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125, authorities said. The train's conductor was among those killed. The Health Ministry gave the casualty toll, saying in a statement that over 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. The crash happened in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo, when a train traveling to southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. The Chief Prosecutor's office said late Sunday its investigators had arrived at the site. An inspection indicated that the crash took place when the Giza-Fayyoum train collided with the last car of the Cairo-Aswan train, which was stationary on the same track and traveling in the same direction, officials said. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government has announced modernization initiatives. Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash happened, said people living nearby rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances. Gamal said that he saw around 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to nearby hospitals. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the cars of the stationary train and were dead when they were pulled out, he said. Outside al-Wasta Central Hospital in Beni Suef province, where some of the injured were taken for treatment, survivors said passengers were in shock and struggling to breathe because of all the dust that was kicked up. Nearby villagers eventually got them out, they said. Farha Gamal, a survivor who was inside the Fayyoum train, said she saw some of the passengers who appeared dead and others were struggling to find their way out of the car. “There were other cars that were completely mangled," she said in an interview. President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post that he ordered a prompt investigation into the crash. Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian Railway Authority said. Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district. Egypt’s deadliest train crash was in 2002, when more than 300 people were killed after a fire broke out on an overnight train journeying from Cairo to southern Egypt. articles.desc: BYD has unveiled its ultra-luxury electric vehicle, the Altior, in Abu Dhabi in an attempt to muscle in on the likes of Rolls-Royce.
articles.content: China's BYD takes on Rolls-Royce with a reported $310,000 four-motor Sedan - BYD | Altior News China's BYD takes on Rolls-Royce with a reported $310,000 four-motor Sedan BYD has unveiled its ultra-luxury electric vehicle, the Altior, in Abu Dhabi in an attempt to muscle in on the likes of Rolls-Royce. targets the ultra-luxury segment and positions itself against established brands. The measures around 18.4 feet long and is effectively a four-seat executive limousine. Yangwang, BYD’s luxury brand, has unveiled the Altior in Abu Dhabi. Expected to be available for pre-order in China at around $311,540 , the new vehicle features rear-hinged coach doors, a four-seat cabin, and a range of bespoke interior and exterior features. BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme Hits 503.17km/h First Production Car Past 500km/h Barrier Also known as the ‘Dingyao,’ the Altior is positioned to compete with other ultra-luxury vehicles like Rolls-Royce Ghost, Mercedes-Maybach S-Class, and Maextro S800.measures around 18.4 feet long and is effectively a four-seat executive limousine. But unlike competitors like Rolls-Royce, BYD’s newIts main selling points include four independent electric motors, one on each wheel. This should give the Altior precise traction and vehicle movement. It also reportedly comes with active suspension, meaning the vehicle uses cameras to detect approaching objects and other obstacles such as bumps. This allows the car’s suspension to anticipate rather than react to road conditions ahead.has a claimed range of 621 miles , though this is based on China’s Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle testing. A more realistic range under the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicle Test Procedure puts the range at something closer to 500 miles , though this has not been officially certified. Cybertruck final countdown: Tesla plans to wind down pickup production in 2027 The Altior reportedly supports charging from 10 percent to 70 percent in approximately five minutes using megawatt-capable chargers, although BYD has yet to confirm the vehicle’s full charging specifications. The Altior’s drivetrain reportedly allows tank turns, crab walking, and stability control following tire blowouts. Of its features, however, the four-motor system is arguably the most interesting and impressive. Conventional cars tend to rely on mechanical systems, brakes, and differentials to provide torque to each wheel. , however, can do this at the wheel directly and, in theory, independently. That allows capabilities such as rotating the vehicle almost on the spot and maintaining directional stability when a tire suddenly loses pressure. Such technology has potentially major implications beyond luxury vehicles, particularly for vehicle safety and off-road applications. These features are impressive, but could the Altior realistically challenge the likes of Rolls-Royce? Technologically, it certainly appears capable of competing. Commercially, however, that’s another question entirely. But Rolls-Royce ownership is more than just buying a piece of hardware; it is seen as a symbol of status and craftsmanship.doesn’t yet have the brand recognition in this area, which is not something you can just “speedrun. ” It takes time. But the bigger picture is that Chinese automotive manufacturers like BYD are no longer satisfied with competing on price and production scale. They’re looking to move into the highest-margin, most prestigious segments of the global industry. And they’re attempting to do so with technology that traditional luxury manufacturers may struggle to match. Whether the gamble pays off remains to be seen, but it will be interesting to see how popular the Altior becomes. articles.title: Democrats won big on Election Day. But can they agree on AI?
articles.desc: Democrats campaigned on concerns about AI and data centers, but competing priorities and opposition from the Trump administration could complicate efforts to enact new regulations.
articles.content: Democrats won big on Election Day. But can they agree on AI? | United States Democrats won big on Election Day. But can they agree on AI? Democrats campaigned on concerns about AI and data centers, but competing priorities and opposition from the Trump administration could complicate efforts to enact new regulations. Skip to ContentDemocrats across the country who swept into power amid growing voter skepticism about AI and data centers are now reckoning with knotty discussions about how to tackle AI regulation and which technological impacts deserve their attention first, according to AI experts, strategists and legislators themselves. Dusted with confetti and batting away Election Day balloons, midterm victors touched on everything from data centers — Sen. -elect Chris Pappas of New Hampshire railed against the facilities that “harm our communities and our well-being” — to healthcare, as Sen. -elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota committed to restricting the use of AI systems in insurance decisions. All of Colorado’s congressional and statehouse races shifted toward Democrats in the 2026 midterms The renewed calls for AI regulation are at odds with President Donald Trump’s insistence that Congress must limit AI-focused regulation or risk hampering American AI innovation. Trump has repeatedly referred to AI as a “golden goose” and data centers as sound economic investments. articles.desc: Sal Jafar, CEO of ESG MENA, sat down with Professor Phil Hart of the Research and Engineering Science Research Centre (RSERC), at the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in the capital…
articles.content: From Scientific Research to Real-World Impact: TII's Innovations in Energy, Water and Food Security - an exclusive conversation with ESG Mena | ESG Mena From Scientific Research to Real-World Impact: TII’s Innovations in Energy, Water and Food Security – an exclusive conversation with ESG Mena From Scientific Research to Real-World Impact: TII’s Innovations in Energy, Water and Food Security – an exclusive conversation with ESG Mena Sal Jafar, CEO of ESG MENA, sat down with Professor Phil Hart of the Research and Engineering Science Research Centre (RSERC), at the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in the capital Abu Dhabi, to discuss how artificial intelligence, advanced materials and engineering innovation are helping address the UAE’s sustainability challenges, from improving solar panel performance and desalination efficiency to strengthening agricultural productivity and reducing energy consumption. As the UAE advances its sustainability and resource-security ambitions, translating scientific research into practical solutions has become increasingly important. At the Technology Innovation Institute’s Research and Engineering Science Research Centre (RSERC), innovation is focused on addressing the interconnected challenges of energy, water, food security and sustainability. Rather than concentrating solely on scientific breakthroughs, the centre adopts an applied-research approach, with an emphasis on technologies that can deliver measurable economic and environmental benefits. Professor Phil Hart explains how this approach is shaping a portfolio of innovations tailored to the UAE’s environmental conditions and resource priorities. Research centres often generate promising scientific discoveries, but translating them into practical applications remains a challenge. How does RSERC approach this gap between research and implementation? Our remit covers energy, water, sustainability and agritech. These areas are closely interconnected, particularly in the UAE, where agriculture and green spaces require significant amounts of water, and much of the water we use is desalinated, making it energy-intensive. Ultimately, our work is about strengthening the country’s energy, food and water security. We do not approach these challenges in isolation; instead, we explore how innovation in one area can deliver benefits across the wider resource ecosystem. Importantly, our objective is not simply to develop interesting scientific discoveries. From the beginning of every project, we consider how the resulting technology could eventually be implemented and commercialised. We continuously assess its potential applications as the research progresses, rather than waiting until the science is complete to consider how it might be used. Let’s start with solar energy. The UAE has considerable solar potential, but extreme UV exposure can affect photovoltaic panel performance. What is RSERC developing to address this? The UAE has an excellent solar climate, and solar energy will play an increasingly important role in the region. However, one challenge is the exceptionally high level of ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which can accelerate the degradation of modern solar panels. Our studies indicate that modern panels can lose nearly 20% of their rated power during their first two years of operation. This represents a significant economic loss and can mean more frequent replacements, creating additional costs and environmental challenges associated with waste disposal. Rather than simply blocking UV radiation, we asked whether it could be converted into additional usable energy. We have developed a molecule that can be incorporated directly into a solar panel. It absorbs high-energy UV photons and subsequently releases visible-light photons, which the panel is designed to convert into electricity. Frederick Amores, DICT Regional Director, Region VII For communities far from major urban centers, reliable mobile connectivity makes a meaningful difference in everyday life. It helps families stay in touch, give students access to more learning resources, and make it easier for residents to connect with government services and online opportunities. PLDT and Smart are working to bring these benefits closer to geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDA) through the rollout of three Smart cell sites in Cebu, Bukidnon, and Cotabato, in collaboration with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), local government units (LGUs), and community partners. The initiative covers Barangay Cansuje in Argao, Cebu; Barangay Cacaon in Talakag, Bukidnon; and Barangay Lampayan in Matalam, Cotabato. Ceremonial switch-on activities took place on October 12, October 26, and October 28, 2026, respectively. The rollout aims to improve access to mobile communication and digital services in underserved areas, opening up more possibilities for education, economic participation, and community development. “Connectivity can make a real difference in people’s lives, especially in communities where access has long been a challenge. For a student, it can mean more opportunities to learn. For a family, it means staying connected. And for local communities, it opens doors to essential services and new opportunities. By working closely with DICT, local governments, and our community partners, we want to help bring these possibilities within reach of more Filipinos,” said Blums Pineda, Senior Vice President and Head of Enterprise Business Group at PLDT and Smart. Connecting communities to more opportunities Beyond bringing mobile connectivity to these communities, the initiative also highlights programs designed to help residents make practical use of digital services. Among these is the Bayanihan SIM Distribution Program, a collaborative effort between PLDT-Smart and DICT that supports the Bayanihan SIM initiative of the Private Sector Advisory Council (PSAC) and DICT. Through the program, residents, students, and other community stakeholders can benefit from connectivity by gaining access to digital platforms, government services, and online opportunities. The initiative recognizes that improving digital inclusion involves helping people access the tools and services that make connectivity useful in their daily lives. “Bridging the digital divide means ensuring that Filipinos, wherever they live, have the opportunity to benefit from technology. Through initiatives such as Bayanihan SIM and our collaboration with PLDT, Smart, and local government units, we are working to make digital services more accessible to unserved and underserved communities. Our goal is to help residents, students, and families use connectivity in meaningful ways, whether for education, access to government services, or opportunities to improve their livelihoods,” said Engr. Pinky T. Jimenez, Assistant Secretary for Infostructure Management of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT). articles.title: Lakewood Radiologist Accused Of $5.2M AI Trading Scheme That Burned Family, Friends
articles.desc: Colorado securities regulators accuse Lakewood radiologist Michael Cole of running a $5.2M Ponzi-like AI trading scheme that targeted family and colleagues.
articles.content: Lakewood Radiologist Michael Cole Sued Over AI Scheme Lakewood Radiologist Accused Of $5.2M AI Trading Scheme That Burned Family, Friends Denver District Court — Reported Filing Site Of Securities Lawsuit A Lakewood radiologist built an investment business pitching an artificial intelligence trading algorithm that he claimed would beat the market year after year. Instead, according to a civil complaint from Colorado securities regulators, the fund lost money every single month for five straight years while the doctor allegedly used fresh investor cash to keep paying off earlier backers. Regulators Allege a Ponzi-Like Pattern Behind the AI Pitch The Colorado Division of Securities alleges that Michael Cole, a radiologist, fraudulently took more than $5 million from investors in an AI investment scheme and failed to deliver the promised returns, according to court filings reported by . Cole created Sage Income LLC in September 2019 and told investors their money would be used to trade stock in a fund he controlled, the complaint alleges. He is not licensed to offer or sell securities in Colorado, according to state officials cited in the filing. Cole allegedly convinced 14 investors to put in a total of $5.2 million through promissory notes in Sage Income, according to the lawsuit, which the Division of Securities filed against him in Denver District Court on November 4, 2026. reported that the commissioner filed the civil fraud charges on November 6, 2026, a discrepancy in reported filing dates that has not been resolved. Cole told investors the AI software had been extensively tested for more than four years and that Sage Income was in good financial standing, the complaint states, and he claimed the software enabled trades generating higher-than-average market returns. Negative Returns Every Month for Five Years, Complaint Says Yellow Scene reported that Sage promoted its proprietary AI software as a securities-trading program capable of generating annual returns between 9% and 15%. Instead, the complaint alleges Sage Income consistently lost money every month from November 2019 through December 2024. State attorneys described Cole's statements to investors as flagrantly dishonest, according to the complaint. Rather than trading gains, Sage Income funded investor payments with cash injected by Cole himself or by new investors, the complaint alleges — the same pattern Yellow Scene described as Cole using investor funds to pay interest to earlier noteholders in what the publication characterized as a Ponzi-like scheme. The complaint further alleges Cole transferred some investor money into his personal account and used investor funds to pay off an unrelated loan. He told state investigators he used investor funds to develop and train the AI software, according to the filing. reported that Cole's personal notes referenced an algorithm error in November 2024 that led to significant losses in about 95% of Sage's accounts. Sage Income filed for bankruptcy in February 2025; its case is listed on . By the time of the bankruptcy filing, investors had lost more than $3.9 million in total, according to the complaint. Before Sage Income, Cole ran Cole Capital LLC with three former business partners, two of whom were members of his own family. The complaint alleges Cole owed those three former partners a combined $1.3 million after Cole Capital was dissolved in 2019 — debt that predated the launch of the fund regulators now say he used to pay off earlier obligations with new investor money. Colorado Securities Commissioner Tung Chan said Cole used the promise of AI investing to defraud Coloradans, including his own brother, parents and colleagues. “We have seen a lot of the same old scams that mask themselves behind the excitement of new technology like AI,” Chan said, urging investors to slow down and research before putting money into anything. Chan recommended remembering that if an investment seems too good to be true, it usually is.

When Ackman disclosed his stake in Uber in February 2025, the company had been under pressure due to fears of what role it would play in a world with autonomous driving. He thought the ride-share company's risk was ultimately limited and that autonomous driving companies were more likely to partner with Uber than disrupt it. James Paxton Revives Late Father Bill Paxton's 1991 Western Role in Last Train to Fortune Meanwhile, he felt its food delivery business would feel no effect, given that a person would presumably have to pick up orders from restaurants and other places and bring them to people's doors. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Ackman added that Uber was "one of the best-managed and highest quality businesses in the world. " Today, investors can buy the stock at a just slightly higher price than Ackman was likely buying shares at nearly two years ago. A large part of Ackman's thesis with Uber is that the company would begin to see strong operating leverage and that profits would nicely outpace revenue growth in the coming years. That has played out, and Uber demonstrated that once again when it reported its third-quarter results on Nov. 4. For the quarter, Uber's revenue increased 10% year over year, to $14.77 billion. That came in ahead of the $14.69 billion consensus, as compiled by. Notably, its mobility segment revenue growth is being affected by new laws in the U.K. and some other European countries that require the company to classify drivers as workers rather than independent contractors. This just affects revenue, so gross bookings is perhaps the better measure of how the company is performing. Both the company's main segments -- mobility and delivery -- reported robust gross bookings in Q2. Mobility gross bookings jumped 18% to $29.5 billion, while revenue fell 2% to $7.5 billion due to the business model change. Segment adjusted, meanwhile, jumped 27% to $2.4 billion. The company saw stable growth in the U.S., while some international markets, like Brazil and India, felt driver supply constraints due to high fuel prices. Delivery gross bookings rose 22% to $28.5 billion, while revenue climbed 23% to $5.5 billion and segment EBITDA soared 30% to nearly $1.06 billion. The company said its grocery and retail business is doing well, with this segment sitting at a $15 billion run rate growing 40%. Showing strong operating leverage in the business, adjusted EBITDA climbed 31% to $3 billion, while adjusted earnings per share jumped 35% to $0.88. Looking ahead, the company forecasts gross bookings to rise between 18% and 22% on a constant currency basis to a range of $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion. It projected that adjusted EPS would increase to a range of $0.95 to $0.88, representing growth of 34% to 39%.
